blocking: PNG IDAT inflation is unbounded: `inflateSync(Buffer.concat(idat))` fully decompresses the stream *before* the `raw.length < (stride+1)*height` guard runs. The compressed file is bounded by the plugin's 64 MiB input cap, but a crafted PNG (this tool's primary input is untrusted client screenshots) can declare dimensions within the 16M-pixel gate while its IDAT stream inflates to hundreds of MB–GBs, OOM-killing the worker or stalling the host. Fix is one line: `inflateSync(Buffer.concat(idat), { maxOutputLength: (stride + 1) * height })` (throws ERR_BUFFER_TOO_LARGE → caught → stats undefined). Same class of issue applies to the `out` buffer allocation and the CSV path is only bounded by timeout. (file="packages/plugin-vision/scripts/vision-worker.mjs", area="resource handling / untrusted input")
non_blocking: Truncated-image parsing yields NaN dimensions: WebP detection only requires 12 bytes but VP8X/VP8 /VP8L branches read bytes 21-29; GIF detection requires 6 bytes but reads bytes 6-9; BMP detection requires 2 bytes but reads bytes 14-25. Tiny/truncated files produce `NaN` width/height that flow into `aspectRatio`, diagnostics, and JSON `null`s instead of a `ParseFailure` error. Add length guards before each variant read. (file="packages/plugin-vision/scripts/vision-worker.mjs", area="correctness")

`chart_generate` overwrite guard is check-then-act: two concurrent calls to the same output with `overwrite:false` can both pass `existsSync` and both write (interleaved/truncated SVG, and the no-overwrite contract is violated). Use an atomic create-exclusive write (or serialize per output path). (file="packages/plugin-vision/src/index.ts", area="concurrency")

Inline `series` items have no per-label length cap and are serialized into argv. 2000 items with long labels can exceed the Windows ~32K CreateProcess command-line limit, surfacing as an opaque ToolFailure. Add a total argv budget or per-label maxLength. (file="packages/plugin-vision/src/index.ts", area="cross-platform")

`chart_generate` accepts both `data` and `series`; `series` silently wins in the worker. Reject the combination or document precedence. (file="packages/plugin-vision/src/index.ts", area="correctness")

Output extension is not enforced: the schema/README say `.svg`, but any path is accepted, so SVG content can be written to `output.png` or an extensionless file. Minor, but the contract is misadvertised. (file="packages/plugin-vision/src/index.ts", area="correctness")

An empty data file (0-byte CSV) returns `ToolFailure: no data rows found` rather than the structured `empty-data` diagnostic the issue's design intends. A header-only file does produce the structured diagnostic, so the zero-row case is inconsistent. (file="packages/plugin-vision/scripts/vision-worker.mjs", area="error handling")

Row 0 is always treated as a header for both analyze and chart, so a header-less CSV silently drops its first record. Should be detected/documented rather than silently lost. (file="packages/plugin-vision/scripts/vision-worker.mjs", area="correctness")

The worker writes to the absolute `--out` path with no knowledge of the workspace root and no re-validation. If a symlink is swapped at the output path between the plugin's `resolveInWorkspace`/`existsSync` checks and the worker's `writeFileSync`, the write follows it (TOCTOU). Boundary enforcement lives entirely in the plugin layer; passing the workspace root to the worker for a final containment check (or writing via a core-owned primitive) would close the gap. (file="packages/plugin-vision/scripts/vision-worker.mjs", area="security / defense in depth")
security: Unbounded PNG inflate (see blocking finding). Reachable by any PNG in the workspace that satisfies bitDepth 8 / non-interlaced / colorType 0|2|6 / width*height <= 16M; the attacker controls the IDAT stream, so decompressed size is not bounded by file size. Fix with `maxOutputLength`. (file="packages/plugin-vision/scripts/vision-worker.mjs", area="resource exhaustion")

The env-allowlist guarantee for `ctx.run` is asserted in comments (`core's DEFAULT_ENV_ALLOWLIST applies`) but `env` is omitted. If core's default were ever to inherit the full environment, harness secrets would reach a worker that parses untrusted files. The behavior is load-bearing; verify against `@dsh-forge/core` and add a test asserting the worker env is not the full parent env. (file="packages/plugin-vision/src/index.ts", area="env allowlist (verification gap)")

The workspace-write and symlink-escape guarantees depend entirely on core's `resolveInWorkspace` realpath behavior. The PR's TDD covers a lexical `..` escape but there is no test that an output path resolving through an in-workspace symlink pointing outside the workspace is rejected (both for read and write). (file="packages/plugin-vision/src/index.ts", area="workspace boundary (verification gap)")
test_gaps: No test for a decompression-bomb PNG (small file, huge inflate) — the one-blocker path.
No test for `chart_generate` permission denial (workspace-write without approval).
No test for the overwrite guard: existing output + `overwrite:false` rejected; `overwrite:true` replaces.
No test for the inline `series` path (only the `data`-file path appears in the TDD evidence).
No test for >64 MiB input rejection, or FIFO/socket/device/directory input rejection.
No test for truncated/malformed images (WebP/GIF/BMP NaN paths, JPEG without SOF, PNG with bad filters).
No test for worker timeout or the 8 MiB output-cap truncation path.
No test for chart edge cases: negative values, single-point pie, pie/area/scatter types, values.length > 2000 via a data file.
No test exercising Windows argv handling (drive-letter absolute paths, quotes/backslashes in task/title, large series JSON).
No test asserting the worker receives only the allowlisted env (see security finding).
compatibility: Load-bearing dependency on `@dsh-forge/core` `resolveInWorkspace` (realpath/symlink semantics), `DEFAULT_ENV_ALLOWLIST`, and `assertPermission`/`ctx.permission` shapes — none are exercised by tests in this PR, and the DeepSeek Harness manifest itself flags the real permission-hook API as unverified against the pinned commit.

The worker relies on `process.execPath` + a committed `.mjs`; this matches the plugin-biome node-shim pattern, but the PR has no CI assertion that the built `dist` entry (`main`/`types` point to `./src/index.ts` while `files` ships `dist`/`scripts`) resolves the worker path correctly when consumed as an installed package.
architecture: Binary detection is reimplemented in-plugin (`resolveVisionWorker` + random-sentinel logic) rather than delegated to a shared `@dsh-forge/core` helper, despite the plugin standard stating binary detection must come from core. If the sentinel/`BinaryNotFound` pattern is duplicated across plugins it should be centralized.

Path parsing/writing is split: the plugin validates and the worker blindly writes to the resolved absolute path without knowing the workspace root. Boundary enforcement should ideally be a core-owned primitive invoked at both layers.

Worker reports non-standard error codes (`UnsupportedFormat`) that `parseWorker` flattens to `ToolFailure`; fine today, but the mapping table should be documented so future worker codes don't silently lose their meaning.
